claim: Average American earned about $1,425 a year, so $1,000 is about eight months' pay
note: Arithmetic on a reported average income.

claim: Dow rose from 63 in August 1921 to 381 in September 1929, about sixfold
About 1.5 million Americans had invested in securities by 1929
Buyers on margin typically put about 10% down and borrowed the rest
note: The doubling and $10,000 lines are arithmetic on 10% margin.

claim: Many brokers required 40-50% margin by mid-1929
note: Secondary source citing Borowiecki, Dzielinski and Tepper; data incomplete.

claim: An RCA pool pushed the stock up almost 50% between 8 and 17 March 1929, then sold; such pools were legal then
note: Single secondary source. 'Everybody wants' is colour, not a statistic.

claim: Dow peak close 381.17 on 3 September 1929
Prices fell about 10% in September then rose about 8% by mid-October
Irving Fisher (Yale) said in mid-October 1929 that stock prices had reached what looks like a permanently high plateau
note: Source confirms the Fisher statement, NYT 16 Oct 1929; wording is the widely quoted phrase, used as paraphrase not as a quotation.

claim: Black Thursday 24 Oct 1929: record 12.9 million shares
Bankers bought shares publicly to steady the market; the effort failed
Black Monday 28 Oct: Dow fell nearly 13%
Black Tuesday 29 Oct: about 16 million shares, Dow down nearly 12%
note: Percent fall from Federal Reserve History.

claim: Margin calls forced sales as prices fell
By mid-November 1929 the Dow was down almost 50%
Recovery looked imminent to contemporaries in 1930; the decline continued to 1932
Dow bottomed 8 July 1932 at 41.22, 89% below the peak
note: $110 is arithmetic on the index, price only.

claim: 1,350 banks suspended in 1930
Bank of United States failed 11 Dec 1930 with about $200 million in deposits, then the largest US bank failure
note: FDIC history confirms the 1930 failure in New York City.

claim: No federal deposit insurance before 1934; runs converted deposits to cash
note: The lunch-hour scene is an invented illustration of a documented pattern.

claim: About 2,300 banks suspended in 1931
About 9,000 banks suspended operations 1930-1933
Depositors lost about $1.3 billion, 1929-1933
Average prices fell by nearly 30% from 1930 to early 1933
Unemployment reached about 25% by 1933
Postal Savings: 2% interest, $2,500 cap, depositors quintupled to 2.3 million by 1933
National bank holiday, March 1933
Banking Act signed 16 June 1933 created the FDIC; insurance from 1 Jan 1934 at $2,500
Deposit insurance removes the incentive to run
Dow regained its 1929 high on 23 November 1954
Insured banks display the FDIC sign
note: FDIC page shows the plaque and seal; 'by the door' is typical, not universal.
